Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0169", "row_sha256": "1c027760a0d2ba46ebfcd126a70536b4eb6e1ebfc59d1b6d608599fbf111851c", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need help putting together an email for the registration desk at the Harborview Open chess tournament. Please address it to Nadia, not Otis. It's about Eli Morgan, who wants to enter the adult open section; he is with East Pier Chess Club. The tournament is on September 14 at Harborview Community Hall, and the registration deadline is September 2. I think the entry fee may be $35, but I haven't confirmed that, so don't present it as a fact. Could the email ask Nadia to confirm the fee and tell us whether Eli's place can still be reserved? Mention that Eli can provide whatever form or payment details are needed, without saying he has paid already or that a place is secured. Keep it fairly brief and courteous, and make clear who the entrant is and which section he wants. Use plain English. I don't need a phone number or background added. Please make it sound like an inquiry, not a confirmation, since we don't have an answer yet. The recipient must be Nadia, not Otis.", "output": "Draft a fairly brief, courteous email to the registration desk for the Harborview Open chess tournament. Address it to Nadia, not Otis. The email concerns Eli Morgan, who is with East Pier Chess Club and wants to enter the adult open section. The tournament is on September 14 at Harborview Community Hall, and registration closes September 2.\n\nAsk Nadia to confirm whether the entry fee is $35, which is unconfirmed, and whether Eli's place can still be reserved. Mention that Eli can provide any required form or payment details. Do not imply that he has already paid or that his place is secured. Keep the email in plain English, clearly identify Eli and his section, and make it an inquiry rather than a confirmation. Do not add a phone number or background."}]
